subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Unimate: The First Industrial Robot
description: A quick, practical guide to Unimate: The First Industrial Robot.

hook.text: In 1961, Unimate became the first industrial robot. It lifted hot metal parts from a die-casting machine at GM.

buildup.text: George Devol and Joseph Engelberger built it. Unimate weighed two tons and moved through stored positions on a drum memory.

discovery.text: It worked in conditions too dangerous for humans — extreme heat, heavy loads, and repetitive toxic fumes.

twist.text: Workers initially hated it. Unions feared job losses. But the robot took the jobs nobody wanted.

climax.text: Engelberger is called the father of robotics. By 1970, Unimate arms populated car factories worldwide.

punchline.text: One arm, one factory, one revolution. Industry was never the same.

quiz.question: What was Unimate's first industrial task?
options: Welding car body panels on a moving assembly line
Lifting hot metal parts from a die-casting machine at General Motors
Painting automobile exteriors with precise spray patterns
